title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ravi Subramanian
description: Motivation: We've observed long-tail latency regressions for low-priority short requests under mixed workloads when the continuous batcher backlog grows. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing behavior, enforce fairness across priority classes, add starvation prevention for small/low-cost requests, and introduce per-request timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking. Changes prioritize correctness and safety (feature gated behind runtime flag) and include targeted benchmarks and unit tests. Summary of changes: - Add priority-aware queue buckets and weighted round-robin selection to reduce priority inversion and prevent single-class starvation. - Implement per-request soft timeouts that trigger a fast-path fallback (serve without waiting for batching) and emit detailed diagnostic events. - Integrate KV cache hit-awareness: requests with warm KV caches get a small priority boost to avoid re-warming costs causing oscillations. - Tune scheduler backoff and batch-size heuristics to reduce excessive queueing under bursty tails (reduced default max_wait_ms, adaptive max_batch based on active GPU pipelines). - Add new metrics and tracing spans: scheduler.queue_depth_by_priority, scheduler.time_in_queue_p50/p95/p99, scheduler.timeout_fallbacks, scheduler.starvation_detected. - Tests: unit tests for bucket logic, integration load test harness with mixed latency/cost workloads, and microbenchmarks showing p99 latency reductions for small requests. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-3421) - [x] Feature flag gated (runtime flag: continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration perf harness run - [x] Release notes added to PR body - [x] Backwards compatible by default runtime flag off in stable releases Runbook notes: If we see increased throughput regressions after enabling, toggle continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2=false and collect scheduler.* metrics for investigation. Migration notes: No API changes. Default behavior unchanged until runtime flag is enabled by infra. Commit summary and files changed are listed below.

small_diffs:
scheduler.py snippet: added weighted round-robin selection loop:
- for bucket in buckets:
-   if bucket.has_ready_batch():
-     chosen = bucket
+ total_weight = sum(b.weight for b in buckets)
+ pick = rng.uniform(0, total_weight)
+ for b in buckets:
+   pick -= b.weight
+   if pick <= 0: chosen = b; break

timeout_fallback.py snippet: fallback emits event and increments counter:
- if waited >= soft_timeout:
-   fall_back_to_fastpath(request)
-   metrics.increment('scheduler.timeout_fallbacks')
review_comments: Marta Lopez (reviewer): Can you add more defensive checks around the weight calculation to avoid zero/negative weights from config? Also please document the expected behavior when all buckets are empty.
Ravi (author): Added defensive clamps in commit c4d2e6b and a unit test that verifies empty-bucket behavior. Documented expected behavior in comments.

Diego Morales (reviewer): We need to ensure the KV cache boost doesn't create oscillation where warm requests always preempt cold ones causing cache churn. Can we make the boost ephemeral and decay quickly?
Ravi (author): KV boost is now implemented as a transient 200ms prize (commit f7e8d9c) and decays; added integration test asserting no increased cache churn over a 60s window.
Emily Chen (reviewer): CI flaked on the integration harness once; can you add a retry around the external harness startup and make sure time-based tests are robust?
Ravi (author): Added retry logic and extended timeouts in the integration harness; CI passed on rerun.
Marta Lopez (approver): Verified perf numbers in benchmark-lab vs baseline. Approving to merge as squash when green.
ci_details: CI pipeline: unit -> lint -> integration-harness -> perf-check
First run: unit passed, lint passed, integration-harness failed (flaky infra), perf-check skipped due to harness failure
Rerun: all stages passed (integration-harness retry added), perf-check completed: p99 latency for small requests improved by ~28% under mixed load (see benchmark-lab job)
perf_summary: Local benchmark-lab run (N=5): mixed workload (50% small low-cost, 30% medium, 20% long) showed p50 ~ unchanged, p95 reduced ~12%, p99 reduced ~28% for small requests. Overall throughput stable within 2% of baseline. Metrics and traces attached to the Linear ticket ENG-3421.
merge_details: Merged by Marta Lopez via squash merge. Merge commit: squash-72011-6f3b1e. Runtime flag default is OFF on main. Changelog entry added to docs/runtime_flags.md and release notes updated.
release_notes: continuous-batcher: scheduler v2 tuning (opt-in via continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2). Improves p99 latency for small requests under mixed workloads by adding priority-aware queues, soft timeouts, and KV-cache-aware scheduling. No default behavioral change until the flag is enabled.
runbook_notes: If enabling scheduler_v2 causes regressions: 1) disable runtime flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2=false 2) collect scheduler.* metrics and trace spans 3) check scheduler.timeout_fallbacks and scheduler.starvation_detected counters 4) revert config weights to conservative defaults and re-enable incrementally
notes_for_oncall: This change is feature gated; oncall should watch scheduler.timeout_fallbacks and scheduler.starvation_detected after enabling. If timeout_fallbacks spike, rollback the flag and collect traces for the affected requests.
audit: Author asserts that this PR has test coverage for the new scheduling heuristics and was run under the benchmark-lab harness; security review not required for this change (no auth surface touched).
